d. Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained:

(1) It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

(2) The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child. Head tilt is acceptable for infants; and

(3) A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

e. Eyeglasses/contact lenses:

(1) Eyeglasses are not acceptable unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons, e.g., the applicant has recently had ocular surgery and the eyeglasses are necessary to protect the applicant’s eyes. A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances. If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:

(a) The frames of the eyeglasses must not cover the eye(s);

(b) There must not be glare on eyeglasses that obscures the eye(s);

(c) There must not be shadows or refraction from the eyeglasses that obscure the eye(s); and

(d) Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.

NOTE: A limited-validity passport using endorsement 46 should be issued when the medical circumstance that requires eyeglasses is temporary and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.

8 FAM 402.1-5 Facial Expression

(CT:CITZ-112; 09-06-2024)

a. The applicant’s expression should be natural. Normal, unexaggerated smiles are acceptable, but unusual expressions and squinting are not.

b. Applicants with physical or mental disabilities, including loss of muscle control (e.g., age-related degeneration or because of a medical condition such as Bell's Palsy), may not be able to produce a natural or unexaggerated expression. You may accept a photograph without a natural or unexaggerated expression in these circumstances. Both of the applicant’s eyes should also be visible and open in the photograph (see the exception for infants in 8 FAM 402.1-1). If the applicant is unable to open one or both eyes because of a medical condition, you may accept the photograph. In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.

expected_units.links: 22 CFR 51.26 is cited for the photograph item.
expected_units.boundaries: Separate the time requirement from the likeness assessment; both may share a claim with explicit components.

source_spans.quote: (6) The photograph must be free of material damage:

expected_units.meaning: Material damage means facial-area damage that destroys good likeness or impedes facial recognition, including eye-area damage.
expected_units.actors: Definition; no acting party is required.

expected_units.scope: Staple holes are an example of non-material facial damage.

review_policy.coverage: Assess only the selected text and stated cross-references. The surrounding full manual pages are context; they do not expand these excerpt coverage targets.
review_policy.boundaries: Multiple units may be represented together if their actors, alternatives, qualifications, and evidence remain distinct and recoverable. One unit may use several linked claims.
review_policy.actors: Literal you is acceptable if preserved as an addressed adjudicator and not replaced by an unsupported specific office. Responsibility context supports a cautious role interpretation, not every unqualified actor assignment.
review_policy.logical_forms: Faithful verbatim logic plus an explicit unresolved issue is acceptable for unsupported logic. Invented executable precision is an error.
review_policy.review_status: Labels and output judgments remain agent-authored until an identified human reviews them.
